description.narrative:
The UNJHRO has identified a number of priorities of action as reflected in its work programme in six pillars (areas of action). These pillars are:
The JHRO country programme includes six focus areas: 1. Strengthening rule of law and accountability for human rights violations JHRO is supporting Congolese authorities in the fight against impunity through technical, logistical and financial support to the military and civilian justice systems. The purpose is to ensure that perpetrators of serious human rights violations and violations of international humanitarian law are brought to justice. As part of this effort actions are also taken to support transitional justice initiatives aimed at consolidating peace and justice among communities.
JHRO is also engaged in the prevention and response to conflict-related sexual violence (CRSV) through the Women Protection Advisors (WPAs) deployed within the JHRO and through it's support to the Senior Women Protection Advisor (SWPA). The latter undertakes high level advocacy to support the FARDC and PNCs implementation of Actions Plans to prevent violations, ensure accountability for perpetrators and assistance to affected survivors.
2. Enhancing and Protecting Civic Space and Peoples Participation JHRO is supporting capacity building and development of policies and programmes towards the promotion and protection of human rights in the DRC. One part of this support targets national human rights institutions while the other aim at strengthening networks of human rights defenders and CSOs involved in defending various human rights.
Joint protection mechanisms are put in place through coordination with protection networks, UN agencies, international NGOs and local partners across the DRC.
3. Enhancing equality and countering discrimination - address leaving no one behind and root causes of inequality
JHRO is also enhancing advocacy with national institutions for inclusion of vulnerable groups, minorities including indigenous people and people with special needs. In addition JHRO is collaborating with the Government on legislation related to the rights of persons with disabilities (PwD) and is supporting advocacy of minority groups such as the need of indigenous people are taken into account in the land reform.
4. Integrating human rights in sustainable development JHRO is paying particular attention on reinforcing understanding, protection and respect of human rights principles and standards, including economic, social and cultural rights (ESCRs) and business and HR principles. Within these efforts special attention is given to marginalized groups and women.
JHRO also has a role in the integration of the human rights norms, recommendations and SDGs with the UNSDCF as well as in the UNCT coordinated responses, including through the Humanitarian Advisory Group and the Triple Nexus.
5. Early warning, prevention and protection of HR in situations of conflict In addition to strengthening the judiciary and ending impunity JHRO also have a mandate to protect civilians and improve their safety, in coordination with MONUSCO civilian and uniformed components, UN and civil society partners. An important part of this work is to continuously monitor the human rights situation and ensure early warning systems that can inform response measures.
JHRO also supported the establishment of FARDC and PNC follow-up committees for human rights violations within their organisations. In addition OHCHR manages a robust database with profiles of personnel from defense and security services which is used help in the screening process before new staff are employed by FARDC. Furthermore JHRO provides training and sensitization for DRC defense and security forces on Human rights due diligence policy and human rights and international humanitarian law.
6. Increasing implementation of the international human rights mechanisms JHRO is also strengthening institutions and CSOs capacity on reporting to the human rights mechanisms through capacity building and sensitization on human rights, to improve their capacity to report to the human rights mechanisms (HRM) and to develop and implement joint workplans.

UNJHRO (JHRO) monitors the human rights situation in the DRC and Sweden has been supporting their office since 2016 with two different contributions. According to the embassy, and the international community at large in DRC, the JHRO is the strongest human rights actor in DRC and therefor the embassy wants to support the office. The JHRO is a joint office between the OHCHR and the human rights section of the Monusco mission in DRC. In addition JHRO is working closely with UNDP in providing training in human rights to the Army and the Police and they are also closely connected in the take-over in the withdrawal of MONUSCO.
Monusco has initiated its drawdown in view of eventually leaving the country. The JHRO branches will stay in many locations and will be one of the last offices to leave. I The grant will be a general support for the country programme however there will be some soft earmarking towards areas that Sweden wants to see prioritised.
The intervention will focus on the following objectives:
1. Strengthening rule of law and accountability for human rights violations 2. Enhancing and Protecting Civic Space and People’s Participation 3. Enhancing equality and countering discrimination - address leaving no one behind and root causes of inequality 4. Integrating human rights in sustainable development 5. Early warning, prevention and protection of HR in situations of conflict 6. Increasing implementation of the international human rights mechanisms

UNJHRO (JHRO) övervakar människorättssituationen i Demokratiska republiken Kongo och Sverige har stöttat sitt ämbete sedan 2016 med två olika bidrag. Enligt ambassaden, och det internationella samfundet i stort i Demokratiska republiken Kongo, är JHRO den starkaste människorättsaktören i Kongo-Kinshasa och därför vill ambassaden stödja kontoret. JHRO är ett gemensamt kontor mellan OHCHR och människorättssektionen i Monusco-uppdraget i Demokratiska republiken Kongo. Dessutom har JHRO ett nära samarbete med UNDP för att tillhandahålla utbildning i mänskliga rättigheter till armén och polisen, och de är också nära kopplade till övertagandet av Monusco.
Monusco har inlett sin neddragning med sikte på att så småningom lämna landet. JHRO-filialerna kommer att stanna på många platser och kommer att vara ett av de sista kontoren som lämnar. Jag Bidraget blir ett generellt stöd för landsprogrammet men det blir en viss mjuk öronmärkning mot områden som Sverige vill se prioriterade.
Interventionen kommer att inriktas på följande mål:
1. Stärka rättsstatsprincipen och ansvarsskyldigheten för kränkningar av de mänskliga rättigheterna 2. Förbättra och skydda det medborgerliga utrymmet och människors deltagande 3. Ökad jämlikhet och motverkande av diskriminering – ta itu med att inte lämna någon på efterkälken och de bakomliggande orsakerna till ojämlikhet 4. Integrera mänskliga rättigheter i hållbar utveckling 5. Tidig varning, förebyggande och skydd av mänskliga rättigheter i konfliktsituationer 6. Ökat genomförande av de internationella mekanismerna för mänskliga rättigheter

UNJHRO has reported many good results for 2024 such as;
51 Partnerships were established and or strengthened. The partnerships engaged aimed at raising awareness on human rights on specific issues and thematics , reinforcing the commitment of these organizations to stand up for human rights and mutualizing efforts in support to state obligation to protect human rights of all.
24 partnerships with CSOs were established or strengthened including two networks of organizations of peoples with disabilities and human rights defenders.
54 womens rights organizations engaged to advance womens rights, counter discrimination and violence.
251 victims of gender- based violence benefitted from assistance with UNJHRO support.
4842 human rights violations and abuses were documented by UNHRO during 2024.
354 visits to places of detention undertaken and 374 unlawfully detained persons released as a result of UNJHRO support and advocacy.
327 human Rights defenders were supported by UNJHRO (Counselling on protection, logistical support, financial support, monitoring and advocacy).
UNJHRO continued its work to fight impunity. Logistical and technical support was provided to military and civil justice authorities, the bar, the victims and witnesses for two Joint Investigation Teams (JIT) and nine mobile courts. UNJHRO continued to play a key role in the protection of victims and witnesses in emblematic court cases before, during and after trials in support of individuals fair trial rights and of a victim-centred approach towards justice. This judicial protection scheme has played a critical role and been instrumental to the success of mobile courts as it enabled 234 victims and witnesses to appear before the courts to testify, including 127 women, 96 men, eight girls and three boys. 195 perpetrators were sentenced in the related trials.
UNJHRO has advocate and provide support for the strengthening of legal and institutional framework for human rights protection and promotion in the DRC. Following the important benchmark marked by the adoption of the law (No 23/027 on the protection and the responsibilities of human rights defenders on 15 June 2023, the Government issued the Arreté Ministériel 0018/ of 25/11/2024 establishing the modalities for the exercise of the activities of human rights defenders in the DRC as an enabling legislation to regulate the implementation of human rights defenders activities.
UNJHRO continued to prioritize training and awareness-raising initiatives in 2024 to enhance compliance with human rights standards. Beneficiaries included Congolese national security and defense forces, regional forces (SAMIDRC), MONUSCO components, and newly deployed contingents.
The UNJHRO continued to provide technical and financial support to local actors, building the capacities of national authorities, the National Human Rights Commission and civil society organizations, and supporting the Inter-Ministerial Committee for Human Rights (CIDH) to improve their interactions with human rights mechanisms.
Since the start of the contribution the following results have been achievied eg.;
Based on its broad human rights mandate with unique expertise and experience in human rights monitoring, investigation reporting and analysis for early warning and policy formulation, UNJHRO has provided during the period in-depth insights to support decision-making and advocacy for the improvement of Human rights situation. From November 2021 to October 2024, UNJHRO registered 8308 incidents and documented 13187 human rights violations and abuses, including 13152 violations and abuses (99%) committed by state authorities and armed groups in conflict-affected provinces.
In the context of progressive disengagement of the MONUSCO, the Swedish support has contributed to strengthen national human rights institutions such as the NCHR for a greater ownership, on effective protection of human rights defenders and widening of the civic space. The support has also contributed to the fight against impunity ,to human rights mainstreaming and strengthening of the collaboration with human rights mechanisms and fostering the integration of human rights in development. In addition, UNJHROs forensic expertise has been an enabler in the fight against impunity.
From 2022 to 2024 the following key results have been achieved: -385 monitoring missions including 240 remote monitoring missions conducted from 15 November 2021 to 31 October - 80 trials and mobile courts supported - 8308 incidents registered and 13187 human rights violations and abuses documented, including 13152 violations and abuses (99%) committed by State authorities and armed groups in conflict-affected provinces. - 1280 visits to detention places conducted - 1557 detainees released, following UNJHRO advocacy efforts including 127 women, 76 minors - More than 613 capacity building training sessions and workshops organized
- More than 6,000,000 persons reached during the 1st edition of the Lusenge Price in promotion of the key role of HRD in general and Women - More than six legislation aiming at reinforcing the legal and institutional framework for the promotion and protection of human rights adopted with UNJHRO support - More than 61 advocacy campaigns undertaken to increase human rights awareness - 24 press releases/statements produced that reached around 600,000 persons
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
